Every chunk reads what the analysis steps left in `derived/` and `figures/`, and computes only what
the report shows. Rendered in the jam-r image (Quarto with knitr).

```{r}
#| label: setup
nca <- read.csv("../derived/nca.csv")
cmp <- read.csv("../derived/model_comparison.csv")
pop <- read.csv("../derived/fit_population.csv")
ex <- read.csv("../derived/exposure_vs_tpp.csv")
```

## Exposure after a single dose

```{r}
#| label: nca-summary
knitr::kable(data.frame(statistic = c("Cmax (mg/L)", "Tmax (h)", "AUC0-24 (mg·h/L)"),
  median = c(median(nca$Cmax), median(nca$Tmax), median(nca$AUC)),
  range = c(paste(range(nca$Cmax), collapse = "–"), paste(range(nca$Tmax), collapse = "–"), paste(range(nca$AUC), collapse = "–"))))
```

## Model

```{r}
#| label: models
knitr::kable(cmp)
knitr::kable(transform(pop, value = round(ifelse(grepl("^l", parameter), exp(estimate), estimate), 4)))
```

![Goodness of fit](../figures/gof.png)

## Planned doses against the target product profile

```{r}
#| label: exposure
knitr::kable(ex, digits = 2)
```

![Steady state at the planned doses](../figures/exposure.png)
